title: Communication-efficient Multi-service Mobile Traffic Prediction by Leveraging Cross-service Correlations

problem.claim: Efficient city-wide prediction of traffic across multiple mobile application services is needed for network management and service provisioning.

gap.claim: Existing approaches treat services independently, fail to exploit cross-service correlations, require historical traffic from all regions, consume substantial bandwidth, and risk prediction failure when regional data are lost.

contributions.claim: CsASTGCN combines cross-service attention with spatial-temporal graph convolution for precise and communication-efficient multi-service mobile traffic prediction.
The framework enables each service to transmit traffic data from only a fraction of regions and uses a masked graph autoencoder to reconstruct missing regional traffic.
A model-based adaptive transfer learning scheme reuses knowledge from existing models to train models for new services without training from scratch.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CsASTGCN and the adaptive transfer learning scheme as novel components.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on a large-scale real-world mobile traffic dataset reportedly show that the model greatly outperforms existing schemes.
The authors report improvements in communication-efficiency and robustness for large-scale multi-service traffic prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Mobile traffic prediction supports network management and service provisioning.
Independent service prediction overlooks correlations and requires costly, failure-prone collection of traffic from all regions.
CsASTGCN uses sparse regional transmission, missing-data reconstruction, and cross-service attention for prediction.
Adaptive transfer learning reuses existing models to accelerate prediction-model training for newly emerging services.
Experiments on a large-scale real-world dataset are reported to outperform existing schemes in communication-efficiency and robustness.
